Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Dev: I’ll be there by 9:15 to move the folding table and put the trolley near the ramp. the ramp is usable, but the right wheel catches on the metal strip, so we should pull the trolley rather than push it down. Facilities said they can’t fix that before Friday.

If rain starts before 10:00, we should ask the driver to unload under the covered loading dock around the corner, then wheel everything through the west corridor. Luis: I’ve asked Omar from facilities to be the second person. He can check the corridor and unlock the freight lift, but he’s covering two buildings, so he may arrive closer to 10. the loading dock is on Quarry Lane, not the alley behind the gallery; the map pin in the old email is wrong.

Nia: thanks, I’ll update the shared calendar with Quarry Lane and the new contact plan. I also found three empty padded bins in storage, which should be enough for the loose tile samples. the bins are labeled “fragile—studio return,” so let’s leave those labels on until the samples are unpacked and logged.

Dev: for the intake paperwork, the invoice lists the replacement value as $2,460, while the carrier sheet shows $2,640. I’ve emailed the studio to confirm which figure belongs on our receipt, and we should leave that field blank until they reply. everything else on the invoice matches the order number, CG-418.

Mara: the gallery opens at noon, and the opening team needs the main aisle by 11:30. If the delivery is still being unloaded at 11:00, we’ll keep the plinths in the receiving bay and bring the smaller cartons through first, as long as the west corridor is open. Don’t put anything in front of the fire panel.

Luis: I can stay until 11:40, but after that I’m due at the kiln room across town. I’ll bring the hand truck, two blankets, and a roll of floor protection; the gallery’s spare hand truck has a loose strap. please message me if the carrier changes the time, since i won’t see updates while I’m driving.

Nia: I’ll take the 9:00 check-in and text the group when I’m at the service entrance. If the truck hasn’t arrived by 10:45, I’ll call the number ending in 2841, then let Mara know before I sign anything. I can stay for the first count, but I can’t be the only person handling the paperwork.

Mara: final note for Thursday: keep the invoice question open, use the corrected Quarry Lane pin, and don’t unwrap the repaired bowls before the conservator arrives.
